prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pearland, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1292; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd prefer to leave my name out of this, since the file is for testing purposes. You can refer to me as the claimant.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was driving on a main road in Pearland, Texas, heading toward a shopping center. Traffic had slowed down ahead of me, so I came to a stop at a light.

Q: What happened next?

A: The car behind me didn't stop in time. I felt a hard jolt from behind and my head snapped back, then forward.

Q: Did you lose consciousness or hit your head on anything?

A: No, I stayed conscious. I didn't hit my head, but my neck and back hurt right away.

Q: Did you get out of your vehicle and speak with the other driver?

A: Yes, we exchanged information. The other driver said they were looking at their phone and didn't see that I had stopped.

Q: Did you seek medical treatment after the accident?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic later that day. They diagnosed a neck and back strain and gave me a prescription for muscle relaxers and some physical therapy referrals.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Yes. My neck is stiff, especially when I turn my head to check mirrors, and my lower back aches after sitting for more than twenty minutes. I've had to cut back on some of my usual activities.

Q: Have you missed any work because of your injuries?

A: I've missed a few shifts and I'm working lighter duties right now. I'm still keeping track of the time I've lost.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: Only that I'm following my doctor's treatment plan and I want this claim handled fairly.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
